purpose.summary: Apply coherent accepted-tip freshness and a shared response budget to the existing confirmed-token HTTP route.
scope: Reuse chronik_runtime_token_info under the native query/mutation gate for both sizing and copying; add no token engine, schema or database.
Use a distinct guarded-query service ABI; preserve older standalone Rust token and transaction service ABIs.
Require accepted-index and active-chain tip agreement before and after token reads, including missing results. Closed, busy or lagging admission returns protobuf 503.
Share one host-query/body permit between token and transaction routes and preserve exactly-once buffer release and shutdown joining.

Exercise both cross-route busy directions, token ownership/error paths and irreversible admission closure after retained-anchor disconnection, with mismatch rejection on restart and explicit reindex recovery.
exclusions: No mempool, history, UTXO, spent-by lookup, websocket, plugin, wallet or full SDK compatibility claim.
No consensus, validation, activation, chain-selection, P2P, network identity or mainnet parameter change.
No duplicate transaction-body store, incoming evidence, private history, host-specific path, binary or cache.

scenarios.command: Run the two-role pruning canary with fresh-pruned bootstrap and concurrent requests during already-indexed pruning.
expected_results: Concurrent old-transaction reads are either canonical 200 or protobuf 503, never a fabricated or partial response. After file removal the old transaction is 503; a retained recent transaction remains 200 and the node continues at its accepted height.
The pre-existing fresh-pruned observer bootstrap failure remains isolated from node correctness.
failure_conditions: Silent 404 for an indexed pruned transaction, fabricated fallback, partial result, node shutdown, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex.
expected_results: Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Experimental confirmed-only local-regtest loopback service. No mempool, history, UTXO, spend-state or full SDK claim.

The older standalone Rust token-only and transaction-query service ABIs preserve their original token behavior; they do not guarantee node active-tip freshness. The node uses the new guarded-query ABI.
Successful and missing responses are snapshots at the final accepted-tip/active-tip check; a later reorganization can invalidate them.
One shared token/transaction body permit bounds concurrent large results; each encoded payload is at most 64 MiB, but parsing and cross-language copies can coexist.
Shutdown joins admitted work to preserve host context; stalled storage or a slow client can still delay graceful shutdown. No hard deadline or formal concurrency proof.
Pruned canonical transaction storage remains unavailable; no duplicate transaction-body store or fallback is introduced.
Zero-value regtest mechanics are not an economically funded profile, historical-chain parity, production deployment or independent reproduction.
Rust dependencies are locked; system/compiler dependencies are declared but not fully locked by Cargo.lock. Local syntax checks do not replace integrated CI.
counterevidence: The existing token handler bypassed the native admission gate. Equality of database tip observations without serialization is not a coherent multi-read snapshot.
The new HTTP test must reject a known token and an unknown token identically while the observer is degraded; an unknown identifier does not justify a stale 404.

The first PR CI run reached deep-reorg restart recovery but refused the HTTP connection. The test incorrectly expected ordinary restart to recover a persistent tip left behind by closed admission; the corrected oracle requires mismatch diagnostics, disabled serving and explicit full reindex. No production recovery behavior is changed.
A shared admission budget intentionally returns 503 for concurrent requests and when observation lags the accepted node tip.
A later reorganization can invalidate a previously correct snapshot; no finality claim is implied.
